title: feat: account-level suspension for under-16 age review
body:
## Summary

- Adds `status` (active/suspended/banned), `suspended_reason`, and `suspended_at` columns to the `users` table
- Auth flow includes `account_status` in UCAN token facts and account status response when non-active
- Service-token admin endpoints (`GET/PUT /api/admin/users/:pubkey/status`) for relay-manager to suspend/unsuspend accounts
- Signer daemon refuses to sign events or encrypt/decrypt for non-active users (DB query per request, no cache)
- Suspended and banned users can still log in to see restriction/ban notices

## Context

Track C of the under-16 system coordination doc. The relay-manager side (case table, state machine, admin queue) and the mobile client (PR #3531 with `restrictedMinorReview`) are already built. This gives Keycast the ability to mark accounts as suspended and enforce that through the signer.

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-18-account-suspension-design.md`

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `bun run db:reset` and verify new columns exist
- [ ] `cargo test --lib` -- all 184 unit tests pass
- [ ] Integration tests for admin endpoints (7 tests in `user_status_admin_test.rs`)
- [ ] Manual: suspend a user via admin PUT, verify `get_account_status` returns status
- [ ] Manual: verify suspended user can still log in but signer refuses `sign_event`
- [ ] Manual: unsuspend user, verify signing works again
- [ ] Verify `KEYCAST_SERVICE_TOKEN` env var is set in staging before deploy

title: chore: Handle duplicate email during OAuth email verification
body:
## Summary

OAuth email verification could give users the wrong result when the pending email was already taken or when two verification attempts raced.
This change checks who owns the tenant email before clearing pending state.
It returns 409 only for a real different-account email conflict and keeps same-account headless retries alive.

> Avoid naming corporate partners, customers, or other sensitive external brands in this PR title or body. Use generic descriptors unless a maintainer explicitly approves the public reference.

## Motivation

The handler checked the pending public key before creating the user, but the database also enforces one email per tenant.
The fix checks email ownership before insert, re-checks it after insert races, and only deletes the pending verification row when another account owns the email.

- Duplicate email conflicts now clear pending verification and return `EmailAlreadyExists`.
- Raw SQL and BYOK duplicate insert paths both avoid treating same-pubkey races as conflicts.
- Race tests use separate committed inserts so rollback behavior does not hide the real owner.

## Related Issue

- Closes #198

## Testing

I ran the Rust checks against the local test database on port 15432.
I also ran the focused verify-email integration tests while developing the race cases.
`git fetch origin` failed because local SSH auth is unavailable, so the rebase used the existing local `origin/main` ref.
